2026-09-09, live: cli.mjs's top-level catch (main().catch((err) => console.error(err.code || err.message))) discards custom error fields (actualResidue, declaredCeiling) on every job it dispatches, not just parcel-r5-zoning -- any future lane needing a thrown error's detail from ANY of this repo's ~25 CLI-dispatched jobs will hit the same defect and must call the job's run function directly, exactly as this dispatch required here.

Two lanes measuring 'the same residue' with two structurally different SQL predicates (point-in-polygon against one population vs. best-overlap-with-fallback against a differently-sourced population) will produce numbers that look comparable and are not. CTX-SP's 48-before/48-after was real data honestly reported, but it was answering a different question than the one CTX-PARCELGATE/CTX-STAMPFALL/CTX-ZONESCOPE were asking. When a dispatch names a specific counting rule 'verbatim', verify that rule is actually the one the consuming system reads before trusting the number it produces.

CTX-SP's CTX-STAGE2-instrument 48-before/48-after discrepancy remains genuinely unresolved -- this lane's own measurement (26, agreeing with the rail's real instrument) does not explain why the OTHER instrument didn't move, only that it was the wrong tool for this particular gate. Per the dispatch's instruction, not chased further here; whoever eventually reconciles CTX-STAGE2's own methodology should know this lane independently confirmed the rail-instrument number is correct and stable, which at least rules out 'the rail's own ceiling is somehow also wrong' as an explanation for CTX-STAGE2's non-movement.
